content: The Institute of Medicine (IOM) is one of the United States National Academies. It is a non-profit, non-governmental organization that was established in 1970 as part of the National Academy of Sciences. Its primary mission is to provide national guidance on issues related to biomedical science, medicine, and health. The IOM operates independently of the government to ensure unbiased analysis and recommendations. It relies on a volunteer workforce composed of scientists and employs a formal peer review system. Each report produced by the IOM undergoes evaluation by external experts, who remain anonymous until the study is published. While the majority of IOM studies are requested and funded by the United States federal government, other organizations also initiate studies, and the IOM itself may independently undertake research. The current President of the IOM is Dr. Harvey V. D. The IOM addresses a wide range of topics, including mental health, child health, food and nutrition, aging, women’s health, education, public policy, healthcare quality, diseases, global health, workplace health, military and veterans’ health, health sciences, environmental health, treatment, public health and prevention, and minority health. The IOM functions both as a research organization and as an honorary membership organization. Its members are elected based on their professional achievements and their ability to contribute to the organization’s mission. These members, along with other experts, volunteer their time without compensation to participate in IOM studies, workshops, and other activities of importance to health. To ensure a diversity of expertise, the IOM’s charter mandates that at least one-quarter of its members be selected from outside the health professions. These members may come from fields such as the natural sciences, social sciences, behavioral sciences, law, administration, engineering, and the humanities. The reports produced by the IOM are made freely available online through the National Academies Press, the publishing arm of the United States National Academies. These reports are accessible in multiple formats.
